title: Image runs as root (no USER configured)
description: The image config declares no USER, so the container defaults to UID 0. Running as root widens the blast radius of any process compromise.
remediation: Create a non-root user in the image and set USER to its UID; verify with `docker inspect`.

title: No HEALTHCHECK configured in image
description: The image config carries no HEALTHCHECK (or it is set to NONE), so runtimes cannot detect an unhealthy-but-running process.
remediation: Bake a HEALTHCHECK into the image that probes the primary process, or define one in the orchestrator.

title: Possible secret baked into image ENV (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
description: Environment variable "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" looks like a credential: the variable name resembles a credential and carries a value. It is readable by anyone who can pull the image and is preserved in layer history.
remediation: Remove the secret from the image and inject it at runtime (orchestrator secret, mounted file, or vault); rotate the exposed value.

title: Possible secret baked into image ENV (DB_PASSWORD)
description: Environment variable "DB_PASSWORD" looks like a credential: the variable name resembles a credential and carries a value. It is readable by anyone who can pull the image and is preserved in layer history.
remediation: Remove the secret from the image and inject it at runtime (orchestrator secret, mounted file, or vault); rotate the exposed value.

title: Image tagged :latest
description: The image reference myapp:latest uses the moving :latest tag; the bits behind it can change between pulls, defeating content verification.
remediation: Tag and deploy images by immutable version, ideally pinning the digest (name@sha256:...) so the running content is verifiable.

title: 2 setuid binaries present
description: The image contains 2 setuid binaries (usr/bin/passwd, usr/bin/sudo). Each runs as its file owner regardless of the invoking user, a classic privilege-escalation primitive.
remediation: Strip the setuid bit from binaries that do not need it (chmod u-s) or remove them; prefer capabilities over setuid where a privilege is genuinely required.

title: 1 setgid binaries present
description: The image contains 1 setgid binaries (usr/bin/wall), which run with their file group and can widen access.
remediation: Remove the setgid bit (chmod g-s) from binaries that do not require it.

title: SSH port exposed by image
description: The image exposes port 22 (SSH). Containers should be immutable and accessed via the orchestrator; a built-in sshd is a lateral-movement foothold and an unmanaged credential surface.
remediation: Remove sshd from the image and drop the EXPOSE 22; use `kubectl exec`/`docker exec` for debugging instead.

title: Privileged port 80/tcp exposed
description: The image exposes privileged port 80/tcp (<1024). Binding it historically required root; prefer a high, unprivileged port and map it externally.
remediation: Expose an unprivileged port (>=1024) inside the container and remap it at the host/orchestrator layer.

title: Sensitive host path declared as VOLUME (/proc)
description: The image declares a VOLUME at /proc, the kernel process filesystem. Persisting this as a mount point steers operators toward binding host-sensitive state into the container.
remediation: Remove the VOLUME declaration for /proc; never mount host kernel/pseudo filesystems or the Docker socket into a container.

title: Incomplete image provenance labels
description: The image is missing OCI provenance annotations (org.opencontainers.image.authors, org.opencontainers.image.licenses, org.opencontainers.image.source, org.opencontainers.image.version). Without them a consumer cannot trace the running image to its source, version, and license.
remediation: Set the standard org.opencontainers.image.* labels (source, version, licenses, authors) at build time.

title: Secret assigned in build history
description: A build step assigned a credential-shaped value. Image history is readable by anyone with the image, so the secret persists even if a later layer removes it.
remediation: Rotate the value. Inject secrets at build time with BuildKit --mount=type=secret (never ENV/ARG) and at run time via a secret store.

title: Remote artifact fetched via ADD during build
description: A build step used ADD with a URL, pulling unverified remote content directly into the image.
remediation: Fetch with checksum verification, or COPY a vetted local artifact.

title: World-writable permissions set during build
description: A build step made files world-writable (chmod 777 / a+rwx). World-writable files let any in-container user tamper with them.
remediation: Grant the least permission the process needs; avoid 777.

title: Remote script piped into a shell during build
description: A build step downloaded a script and executed it unverified (curl|sh) — a supply-chain injection point baked into the image lineage.
remediation: Download to a file, verify a checksum or signature, then execute.

title: Package manager present in runtime image
description: The image ships package manager(s): apt-get. In a runtime image these are attack surface — they let an attacker install tooling — and signal that build dependencies were not pruned.
remediation: Use a multi-stage build so the runtime stage carries no package manager, or switch to a distroless/minimal base.

title: Shell present in image
description: The image contains shell(s): sh. A shell is the usual pivot for command injection and post-exploitation; shell-less (distroless) runtimes deny that primitive.
remediation: If the application does not need a shell at runtime, move to a distroless/scratch base so no shell ships in the final image.

title: Sensitive file deleted in a later layer is still recoverable
description: The image adds app/secret.key in one layer and removes it in a later one, but the delete is only a whiteout marker: the original bytes remain in the earlier layer and can be recovered by unpacking it.
remediation: Never add a secret to any layer. If one was committed, rebuild the image from a clean history (BuildKit secret mounts / multi-stage) and rotate the exposed credential.
